extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature — scientists, engineers, and scientific professionals (general scientific public and institutional administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: Short news items, announcements, and research summaries published in a scientific magazine (Nature) intended to inform researchers, practitioners, and administrators across multiple scientific disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibition: illustrate scientific principles of wind-flight
rubrics_metrics.description: The exhibition will be the attempt to illustrate the scientific principles underlying wind-flight, both as regards the results already achieved and the problems that yet remain to be solved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to showing the wings of such birds as the albatross, eagle, condor, etc., the promoters will illustrate the way in which the presence of wind renders motorless flight possible. Identify and demonstrate the three types of helpful winds: (1) vertical convection currents due to sun’s heat; (2) upward currents due to undulations in the ground (hills and valleys); and (3) varying horizontal currents. Use examples (recent flights) to show application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Film record standards for high-altitude expedition documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: A film record of the Mount Everest Expedition should be of exceptional interest and permanent value as a record of life in Tibet and the conditions of mountain exploration in 1922.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include subjects such as scenery of forest belt, Tibetan plateau, mode of life of Tibetans, Rongbuk monastery and ritual dances, approach to Mount Everest via Rongbuk glacier, assaults by climbing parties, and effects of high winds. Overcome technical difficulties of high-altitude filming (films freezing when wet, sparking when dry, dust contamination) by developing film on-site where necessary (e.g., tents, improvised dark rooms). Use telephoto lenses to capture distant action (descent/ascent of climbing parties). Arrange public showings and allocate proceeds appropriately (e.g., to fund further expeditions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant application procedure — Andrew Carnegie Research Fund
rubrics_metrics.description: The Iron and Steel Institute will receive applications for grants from the Andrew Carnegie Research Fund in aid of research work on the metallurgy of iron and steel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must be submitted before the specified deadline (before the end of February) and must be made upon a special form obtainable from the secretary. Follow the institute's prescribed form and timetable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hiring qualifications — Director of Norfolk Agricultural Station
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for the director post must possess a modern scientific training in agriculture, with university degree or diploma, practical knowledge of mixed farming, organising ability, and be qualified to lecture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appointment initially for one year; remuneration and expenses specified (annual value of 600/., plus travelling and incidental expenses). Applications should include testimonials and be sent to the named honorary secretary by the stated deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization of biological bibliography and abstracts
rubrics_metrics.description: To meet research-student needs there should be sufficient abstracts published in book-form, with adequate indexes — 'the complete subject index being perhaps of the greater importance.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate publication on the lines of Chemical Abstracts; federation of the Biological Research Associations is a necessary preliminary; ensure adequate support via guaranteed circulation so composition costs are covered (composition cost relatively small compared with paper, machining, binding, distribution). Anticipate large literature volume (likely greater than pure/applied chemistry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocacy criterion for adoption of the metric system
rubrics_metrics.description: The metric system is the international language of quantity and should be adopted to avoid confusion caused by diverse weights and measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point to increasing obligatory adoption (46 countries), with practical arguments: electrical science, wireless communication and aviation already use metric units (e.g., wave-lengths in metres); list current divergences among English-speaking nations (US standard gallon 231 in³ vs Imperial 277.274 in³; cental vs Imperial cwt; short ton vs long ton). Conclude that adoption of metric is the simplest way to avoid confusion; sustained campaigning by Decimal and American Metric Associations will eventually succeed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative transport evaluation metric — cost per ton-mile at normal speed
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate transport agencies by estimated cost per ton-mile at their normal speeds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use comparative figures (examples given): barge 1 mph ~ 0.0004/., London motor omnibus 10 mph ~ 0.016/., electric passenger train (3rd class) 25 mph ~ 0.018/., steam train 40 mph ~ 0.024/., liners and class differences (1st/3rd), London–Paris passenger aeroplane (assumed 100 mph) cost estimates vary (0.33/. vs Advisory Board estimate 0.71/.), Rolls‑Royce car running cost assumptions, parcel post, letters, postman per ton-mile, rigid airship estimates dependent on speed and assumed load. Note figures may be official or estimated — consider assumptions (speed, load) when comparing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards and education recommendations for illuminating engineering
rubrics_metrics.description: Closer co-operation between architects and illuminating engineers and inclusion of artificial lighting instruction in architectural curricula are recommended to improve lighting of public buildings and schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite benefits from collaboration of medical profession and lighting experts in dealing with effects of light on the eye. Make use of scientific measurements of daylight illumination (relevant in legal judgments on access of light and air). Promote development and exhibition of practical instruments (e.g., simple illumination photometer, improved inspection lamps) and novel lighting technologies (signs using total internal reflection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory testing standards for stone preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish stone types (limestone; sandstone with calcite cement; sandstone with silica cement) and apply different laboratory test methods with a suggested preservative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design complete laboratory tests appropriate to the stone type; evaluate new preservative preparations (e.g., one that deposits hydrated silica as a cement between particles) by experiments and photographic documentation; Royal Institute of British Architects encouraged to experiment with promising preservatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological caution in physiological/experimental surgery studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid hasty conclusions about internal secretions when observed effects may be produced by injury or disease extending beyond the targeted organ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure surgical or experimental procedures avoid inadvertent damage to neighbouring brain regions (e.g., small injury to the hypothalamus can produce symptoms commonly attributed to pituitary damage). Use careful operative technique and controls to localize effects before attributing them to a particular organ or internal secretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research priorities and methods for cotton improvement (Egypt)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research to improve cotton crops should address decline in yield, rotation length (two-year vs three-year), control of seed used for sowing, and methods to control diseases and pests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate summer fallow benefits (surface soil temperature and partial sterilisation), reassess the fertilising value of Nile silt, study effects of reduced watering on yield and quality, work on extraction of pure lines, propagation of selected strains, and field tests of commercial varieties. For disease control (e.g., sore-shin) and pests (pink boll-worm, cotton-seed bug), test reagents for seed soaking and sowing date effects; recognize that large-scale applicable solutions may be challenging and require field-scale validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desirable content and quality for marine biology papers
rubrics_metrics.description: High-value contributions include detailed descriptions (illustrated by photographs) of previously poorly-known life stages or structures (e.g., egg capsules and young of rays and skates) and useful parasitology life-histories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide excellent illustrations/photographs, fill clearly identified gaps in knowledge (food organisms of young edible fishes, life-history of parasites), and aim for papers that are both descriptive and well-illustrated to meet community needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photometric observation and analysis standards (Uranus brightness study)
rubrics_metrics.description: Photometric studies should use careful series of magnitude determinations reduced to a standard (e.g., mean opposition), with estimation of probable errors and grouping by relevant physical periods (e.g., rotation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ skilled observers and reliable instruments (e.g., Zeiss field-glass); use comparison stars (e.g., Harvard magnitudes) and apply small nightly-error estimates (example: probable error per night 0.04 mag, mean <0.01 mag). Group observations according to rotation period and fit sinusoidal curves, but treat very small amplitudes (e.g., 0.02 mag) with skepticism unless supported by confidence. Consider alternative methods (e.g., apsidal motion of inner satellites) as potentially more trustworthy measures of physical parameters like oblateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial standard: avoid publishing unsupported speculative physical explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not publish speculative suggestions that are physically implausible or of negligible magnitude without commentary, as they may mislead readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess quantitative plausibility (e.g., bending of grazing sunlight by Earth's gravity at surface is ~1.75/3000 of an arcsecond — negligible) before printing speculative claims; if published, accompany with critical comment to prevent misleading weighty journals' readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archaeological field-search strategy recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust excavation search priorities based on likely survival/evidence (e.g., look for dovecots rather than shrines to find Roman dovecots).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When expected features are not being found (few dovecots discovered), alter search focus and methods (seek structural foundations or pigeon-holes) to increase chances of discovery; consider alternative hypotheses about site use and longevity when interpreting finds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research methodology for diurnal temperature variation studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Study diurnal variation of temperature as affected by wind velocity and cloudiness using observations from multiple stations (e.g., Eiffel Tower and Parc St. Maur).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine observations from tall meteorological platforms and nearby standard sites to estimate the magnitude of diurnal temperature rise and range under varying wind and cloud conditions; use coordinated observational datasets to isolate effects of wind velocity and cloud cover.
